verdicts.factCheck: I fetched uint256.hpp from main and from v0.16.7 on raw.githubusercontent.com. Main is 75,879 bytes and contains the word barrett 21 times. v0.16.7 is 37,912 bytes and does not contain it. The Barrett code sits in namespace barrett (line 1383 on main). The division-based mulmod is at lines 955-962 and calls udivrem on wide_mul. runtime/math.hpp on main calls the unqualified mulmod and addmod on uint256_t (lines 74-96) and has no using-declaration for barrett, so the handler resolves to the division-based function. emitter.cpp on main has no use of barrett, reciprocal or mulmod_const. touched_memory_end_ is reset in begin_new_block (line 1042) whenever the block does not continue the previous stack, and is read and set at lines 6348 and 6355. Memory::offset_bits is 28 (runtime/types.hpp line 126 on main), so static_cast<int32_t>(lit) + read_size cannot overflow to a negative end that would wrongly pass the comparison. The emitter on main calls asmjit::imm(runtime_fun_) at line 525. At v0.16.7, cmd/monad/main.cpp line 488 picks InterpreterOnly when trace_calls is set, and rpc/monad_executor.cpp line 1309 fixes eth_call to InterpreterOnly. The releases page lists v0.16.7 with mainnet N/A and testnet 2026-11-19, and v0.16.5 with mainnet 2026-10-22. The asynchronous execution page says the delayed merkle root is 3 and that a block with a wrong delayed merkle root is rejected. web3_clientVersion on rpc.monad.xyz returned Monad/0.16.7. debug_traceTransaction with callTracer on that endpoint returned a stored frame for a transaction in finalized block 125,607,628, whose timestamp equalled the local clock.
verdicts.codeCheck: src/libraries/FullMath.sol:24 runs mulmod(a, b, not(0)) on every mulDiv. src/libraries/FullMath.sol:48 and :112 and src/libraries/SqrtPriceMath.sol:252 run mulmod with a variable denominator. src/libraries/CustomRevert.sol:16-43 writes at fixed offsets 0x00 and 0x04. src/libraries/Hooks.sol:144 reads the free memory pointer at 0x40, and src/types/Currency.sol:57 does the same. An ordinary account can reach all of these with an ordinary swap, but the swap only reaches a fault if validators run a faulty release. On the code as tagged no such fault is shown, and the main-branch paths I read give the same results as the tagged code.

clearedSpotChecks.check: Whether the Barrett reduction added to uint256.hpp on main reaches any EVM opcode handler.
clearedSpotChecks.note: math.hpp on main calls the unqualified mulmod and addmod on uint256_t. The Barrett overloads sit in namespace barrett, and math.hpp has no using-declaration for that namespace, so name lookup reaches the division-based functions at uint256.hpp lines 921 and 955-962. emitter.cpp on main does not name barrett, reciprocal or mulmod_const. I did not read every one of the 109 files, only math.hpp and emitter.cpp, which hold the MULMOD and ADDMOD paths.

clearedSpotChecks.check: Whether v0.16.6 runs different VM code from v0.16.5 or v0.16.7.
clearedSpotChecks.note: The jsDelivr flat listings for v0.16.6 and v0.16.7 give identical hashes for every file under category/vm, category/core/runtime and category/execution/ethereum/state3. Under those prefixes 23 files differ between v0.16.5 and v0.16.6. The finding counts 28, likely over a wider prefix set. The count is different, but the conclusion that v0.16.6 equals v0.16.7 holds.

clearedSpotChecks.check: Whether public endpoints and validators can disagree silently about a PoolManager result.
clearedSpotChecks.note: rpc.monad.xyz answered debug_traceTransaction with callTracer, which needs stored frames and therefore trace_calls, so the node uses InterpreterOnly (main.cpp line 488 at v0.16.7). Its finalized block 125,607,628 had a timestamp equal to the local clock. The asynchronous execution page says blocks with a wrong delayed merkle root are rejected. A divergence between the interpreter and native code would therefore show up as the tracing nodes failing. It would not stay hidden. This does not stop validators from applying a faulty native result, as the finding says.
